This matter is taken up through Hybrid Arrangement (Virtual /Physical Mode).
2.
Heard learned counsel appearing for the Petitioner and learned Additional Standing Counsel appearing for the State-Opposite Party.
Perused the materials placed before this Court.

3. The present bail application under Section 439 of Cr.P.C. has been filed by the Petitioner for regular bail in connection with G.R. Case No.364 of 2024, arising out of Banpur P.S. Case No.241 of 2024, pending in the Court of learned J.M.F.C., Banpur for alleged commission of offence punishable under Sections 419 / 420 / 468 / 471 of I.P.C.
4.
Learned counsel for the Petitioner submits that earlier this matter was not before any other Bench of this Court.
It is submitted by the learned counsel for the Petitioner that the Petitioner is in custody since 26.07.2024.
He further contended that in the meantime the investigation has progressed substantially in the meantime.

He further referring to the allegations made in the F.I.R.,
learned counsel for the Petitioner submitted that the Petitioner has been falsely implicated in the present case.
He further submitted that the Petitioner is ready and willing to return the money that has been paid through his account that is the tune of Rs.2,00,000/-.
He further submitted that the Petitioner has no intention to cheat the informant in any manner whatsoever.

He further contended that the Petitioner does not have any similar criminal antecedents and he belongs to the locality,
therefore, there is no chance of absconding.
In such view of the matter, learned counsel for the Manas Barik vs State Of Odisha .....

Petitioner submitted that the Petitioner be released on bail on any terms and conditions deemed fit and proper by this Court.
5. Learned Additional Standing Counsel on the other hand opposed the bail application of the Petitioner on the ground that the investigation is still on.
Further submitted that in the event the Petitioner is released on bail, he might indulge in similar criminal offences.
Therefore, on such ground, learned counsel for the State submitted that the bail application of the Petitioner be rejected at this juncture.

6. Having heard learned counsel for the respective parties and on careful consideration of the surrounding facts as well as materials on record, further undertaking given by the Petitioner to refund the money that has been transferred to his bank account, this Court is inclined to release the Petitioner on bail subject to imposition of stringent conditions.

7. Hence, it is directed that the Petitioner be released on bail in the aforesaid case on furnishing a bail bond of Rs.30,000/- (Rupees Thirty thousand) with two solvent sureties each for the like amount to the satisfaction of the learned court in seisin over the matter.

Release of the Petitioner shall be subject to the following conditions that:-
I. shall not indulge in similar type of offences while on bail; and II. shall cooperate with the investigation and appear before the Investigating Officer as and when required for the purpose of investigation.
III. shall refund the amount which has been paid to his account to the tune of Rs.2,00,000/- within a period of two months.
Violation of any of the terms and conditions shall entail cancellation of bail.
8. It is further directed that the bail granted to the petitioner is subject to verification of criminal antecedent.
In the event, the Petitioner is having any similar criminal antecedent, then this order stands automatically revoked.
9. The BLAPL is, accordingly, disposed of.
( A.K. Mohapatra) Judge Anil Location: High Court of Orissa Manas Barik vs State Of Odisha .....
